name: Accessible participation formats and barrier reduction
definition: Offer diverse participation modes (written, roundtables, in‑person) in accessible venues and identify/mitigate institutional, technical, procedural, and social barriers to online participation.

name: Acquisition planning, methods, and post‑award controls
definition: Formulate acquisition strategies, select appropriate contracting methods/options, plan for controllable cost drivers and risks, monitor costs, and maintain effective post‑award controls aligned with productivity and fair competition.

name: Actionable alternatives and drafting in public comments
definition: Comments propose specific, feasible in‑scope alternatives or ready‑to‑adopt regulatory text (including mitigations), with clear, concrete asks that staff can implement.

name: Adds new, material information to the record
definition: Introduce new, relevant facts, evidence, analysis, or perspectives the agency has not already addressed, expanding the scope and value of the administrative record.

name: Adequacy and clarity of rulemaking notices and disclosures
definition: Notices clearly describe the action, subjects/issues/terms, intended effects, and any information to be collected (with purposes), enabling meaningful, informed public comment.

name: Administrative and respondent burden minimization and efficiency
definition: Reduce unnecessary administrative, reporting, and procurement burdens; document concrete efficiency gains; tailor compliance (e.g., small entities); and use technology to minimize respondent effort.

name: Algorithmic and data‑system safeguards, privacy, and human oversight
definition: Require human alternatives/fallback and review; ensure explainability/contestability; embed privacy/data‑protection (minimization, purpose limits, user control, secure dissemination); and provide due process, independent evaluation, and accountability.

name: Alternatives analysis rigor (options, instruments, and baseline)
definition: Identify and evaluate a manageable but meaningful set of reasonable alternatives—including non‑regulatory instruments and design variants—against a well‑defined baseline; clearly compare trade‑offs.

name: Analyze distribution of costs and benefits
definition: Identify who bears costs and who receives benefits and treat distributional impacts as decision‑relevant.

name: Authorship and identity authenticity and provenance
definition: Ensure content is genuinely authored with proper attribution, the commenter’s identity is authentic/verifiable, and funding/sponsorship or coordination is transparently disclosed; discourage inauthentic campaigns.

name: Benefit‑cost analysis quality and methodological rigor
definition: Analyses use clear baselines; quantify and qualitatively assess benefits and costs for main alternatives; make assumptions transparent; include non‑quantified effects; apply accepted methods (including sensitivity/alternative cases) with appropriate precision.

name: Best‑available evidence, science, and methodological transparency
definition: Base analyses and decisions on the best reasonably obtainable scientific and technical information, with transparent models, data, and appropriate peer review.

name: Campaign authenticity, coalition transparency, and mass‑comment signals
definition: Disclose funding/coalitions, avoid astroturfing, design mass campaigns to add investigatory value (pairing volume with a substantive umbrella submission), and identify duplication/coordination signals.

name: Chemicals regulation submissions and OEL consultations
definition: Prepare robust chemical submissions (e.g., SNUNs) with exposure/hazard data and engage in Occupational Exposure Limit consultations by providing relevant evidence and analysis.

name: Civic education and engagement capacity
definition: Build relevant, engaging civic knowledge and deliberative skills (including propaganda/error detection), strengthen feedback loops, and support meaningful public participation.

name: Clarity and sufficiency of consultation materials
definition: Provide plain‑language, concise consultation materials that clearly state the questions being asked and include only the information needed for informed responses.

name: Clarity on consultation scope and objectives
definition: Explicitly state what issues are open for comment and the consultation’s objectives within the notice/RIS.

name: Clear stance and specific, actionable recommendations
definition: State a clear position early; make concrete, text‑level recommendations (with timing where relevant); structure claims–evidence–reasoning–remedy; and conclude with a focused ask.

name: Clear, plain‑language executive summaries and overviews
definition: Provide concise, accessible explanations of what is proposed, why, and anticipated impacts to enable meaningful public input.

name: Climate‑risk and emissions disclosure transparency
definition: Ensure clear, consistent disclosure of climate‑related risks, targets, methodologies, progress, and emissions to support accountability and prudent risk management.

name: Coalition affiliation and breadth in sign‑on letters
definition: Disclose coalition/joint‑letter participation and demonstrate breadth and diversity of co‑signers across stakeholder types and levels.

name: Coalition strategy, credibility, and record‑building
definition: Coordinate positions with allies, cite each organization’s distinct expertise, and use iterative engagement to build a coherent administrative record.

name: Comment organization, clarity, and usability
definition: Make comments easy to use: clear structure and flow (executive summary, section‑by‑section analysis), concise plain language, audience‑appropriate presentation (e.g., agency/OIRA/courts), and a dedicated analysis section with evidence.

name: Comment specificity, relevance, and targeting
definition: Stay within scope, use a professional tone, focus on decision points, be concise, and target specific provisions/questions rather than offering generic or irrelevant material.

name: Comment structure, organization, and summaries
definition: Provide a clear introduction stating identity/relevance; an upfront summary of key points; organized sections with headings/bullets and logical flow; and a brief concluding recap/close.

name: Commenter identity, stake, and qualifications
definition: Clearly identify who the commenter is, whom they represent, why they’re affected, and relevant expertise or lived experience; indicate breadth of support or represented constituencies where applicable.

name: Competition impacts and antitrust safeguards
definition: Evaluate potential anticompetitive effects and discriminatory impacts and adopt safeguards to preserve competition.

name: Comprehensive impact assessment scope
definition: Cover economic, social, environmental, safety, and distributional effects (including unintended consequences), using qualitative assessment when quantification is difficult.

name: Concision and focus
definition: Keep the submission succinct, tightly focused on the rule, and easy for staff to excerpt and address.

name: Concrete, context‑specific, domain‑aware impact evidence
definition: Provide detailed, real‑world examples and technical specifics; localize who/where is affected; include sector‑specific data and practitioner insights to show concrete harms/benefits and implementation implications.

name: Consultation purpose, scope, mechanisms, and accessibility
definition: Clearly define consultation purpose/scope, specify the feedback sought and its use, and provide accessible materials/mechanisms (including for LEP and diverse participants).

name: Cross‑jurisdictional consistency, cooperation, and interagency coordination
definition: Align methods and assumptions, avoid duplication, clarify legal interactions, and institutionalize interagency collaboration, information sharing, and recognition/standards across jurisdictions.

name: Direct engagement with the proposal and analytic record
definition: Comments address specific questions and regulatory text, cite the notice and support analyses, and raise issues requiring a substantive agency response.

name: Directly respond to the agency’s specific questions and prompts
definition: The comment explicitly answers the notice’s questions and requested topics, provides responsive data/evidence, and clarifies if requests are inapplicable or immaterial.

name: Disaggregate and segment impacts by affected populations and stakeholders
definition: Identify impacted groups and geographies and provide disaggregated, quantitative impact estimates by relevant segments.

name: Employee parking and commuting policy design
definition: Design parking/pricing and car/vanpool policies to recover costs, incentivize pooling and conservation, minimize administrative burden, respect mission/security and overtime realities, and address off‑hours/irregular‑shift constraints.

name: Engagement with RIA and economic analysis
definition: Comments directly engage the agency’s RIA/economic analysis—citing methods and assumptions, challenging baselines and estimates, and, where useful, offering tractable alternatives analysis.

name: Engagement with agency rationale, record, and significant issues
definition: Demonstrate understanding of the proposal, address the agency’s stated rationale, mandate, and questions, and analyze significant issues the agency must resolve for the final rule and review.

name: Environmental impact scope and territorial context
definition: Identify direct, indirect, offsite, and regional/territorial environmental effects, including cumulative or sector‑wide impacts and EJ dimensions.

name: Environmental justice analysis and equitable program design
definition: Assess and mitigate disproportionate environmental impacts on underserved communities, gather local data via engagement, and embed EJ in permitting/program design with mechanisms to direct benefits and ensure access.

name: Equity and distributional analysis of impacts
definition: Make distributional consequences explicit, assess equity and fairness across subgroups (including EJ/accessibility where relevant), use representative data, and describe mitigation.

name: Evidence‑supported, verifiable claims
definition: Make specific, checkable assertions supported with credible evidence and clear citations to sources (preferably independent/scientific where relevant).

name: Evidentiary rigor and sourcing in comments
definition: Arguments are grounded in specific, credible evidence with clear sourcing and documentation; methods are appropriate; uncertainty is acknowledged; avoid uncited claims and overreach.

name: Evidentiary support and argumentation quality
definition: Present clear, structured claims backed by credible, peer‑reviewed or empirical evidence; use citations and concrete examples; maintain high signal‑to‑noise; anticipate/rebut counterarguments.

name: Fair notice, precision, and clarity of legal obligations and guidance
definition: Ensure rules and guidance give persons of ordinary intelligence fair notice of duties, use precise terms that constrain discretion, and provide timely statements of basis/purpose and clarity at issuance.

name: Identify overlooked or uncounted impacts and cost drivers
definition: Show where the agency missed important aspects or failed to count indirect/hidden costs or benefits, and document additional cost drivers.

name: Implementation feasibility, practicality, and timelines
definition: Address operational feasibility, compliance burdens and costs, realistic transition timing/phasing, and resource constraints; propose workable approaches.

name: Inclusive participation access and targeted outreach
definition: Ensure broad, unbiased access (ADA/LEP supports), prioritize outreach to affected and most‑impacted groups, clarify participant roles/rights, address barriers to participation/adoption, and enable citizen enforcement where relevant.

name: Least‑burden, proportionate regulatory design
definition: Tailor requirements to minimize burdens consistent with achieving objectives, avoiding disproportionate impacts.

name: Legal effectiveness and record‑building posture
definition: Use precise, legally salient arguments that engage the agency’s reasoning, surface logical‑outgrowth or notice issues, pinpoint required decision points, and preserve issues for judicial review to trigger response duties.

name: Limits on legitimate coercion by state and society
definition: Interference with individual liberty is justified only on defined grounds (e.g., preventing harm to others); reject arbitrary power and guard against political or social tyranny.

name: Management planning, performance measurement, and M&E transparency
definition: Set strategic/management goals, plan for evidence collection and use, track/report measurable results, and make monitoring information publicly available (with appropriate protections).

name: OGP action‑plan co‑creation, commitments, and learning
definition: Ensure genuine co‑creation/outreach, include specific/time‑bound/measurable commitments with full problem–solution–results descriptions, and scale ambition with learning across action‑plan cycles.

name: Open‑government principles with inclusive stakeholder engagement
definition: Advance transparency, participation, and accountability tailored to context, moving beyond data publication to genuine inclusion of stakeholders (including subnational and research actors).

name: Open‑network user rights and information
definition: Ensure users can access content, run applications, attach devices, and receive meaningful service‑plan information, subject to lawful constraints.

name: Originality and distinctiveness of submissions
definition: Comments are authentically written and substantively distinct (not form letters), with an original voice, unique data or analysis, and personalized substance; avoid bare, unsupported opinions.

name: Outcome‑focused performance objectives and metrics
definition: Define objectives in terms of ultimate outcomes; select outcome‑oriented indicators; and use multiple complementary metrics with stated limitations.

name: Outsourcing suitability, workforce protections, and capability retention
definition: Assess when to outsource, protect workforce rights/procedures, manage security risks, and retain essential organic capabilities within government.

name: Parking and commute access fee policy design
definition: Design and evaluate parking/access fee policies to recover space costs, reduce hidden subsidies, set fair rates, ensure reliability and nondiscrimination, provide reasonable exemptions (e.g., for no-viable‑alternative or duty-required solo driving), and manage administrative and equity impacts.

name: Participation process quality, authenticity, transparency, and capacity
definition: Design participation to be timely, meaningful, and well‑resourced; avoid tokenism; use transparent e‑rulemaking/records; disclose how input informs policy; build MEL capacity; and report outcomes accessibly.

name: Personalization and substance in mass‑comment campaigns
definition: Avoid duplicative form letters and easily detectable templating; enable and submit unique, substantive, human‑authored comments (AI assistance is acceptable when transparently, genuinely used).

name: Plain, accessible language
definition: Use clear, plain English; avoid jargon and unexplained acronyms; define necessary technical terms so non‑experts can follow.

name: Plain‑language clarity and user‑centered regulatory communications
definition: Draft rules, guidance, and supporting materials in plain language with clear organization and formatting; ensure usability and accessibility for diverse users, minimizing ambiguity and cognitive burden.

name: Pluralism as a safeguard against faction and majority tyranny
definition: Liberty is protected by a multiplicity of interests and associations in a large republic that checks domination by factions.

name: Predictability, uniformity, and reduced uncertainty in compliance
definition: Promote predictable, uniform application/enforcement and, where suitable, national standards and structures that reduce compliance uncertainty.

name: Prefer performance‑based, flexible regulatory approaches
definition: Favor outcome‑based, non‑prescriptive designs that give entities flexibility in how to comply while maintaining effectiveness.

name: Privacy, confidentiality, and public‑posting guidance
definition: Warn that comments become public records; avoid PII or proprietary/sensitive content; handle contact information per notices; and protect confidential sources/methods where applicable.

name: Professional, civil tone and appropriate content
definition: Maintain a respectful, professional tone; avoid personal attacks, threats, or indecent/obscene material.

name: Progress on R&D of advanced ADP systems
definition: Report and assess progress on research and development of advanced automatic data processing (ADP) systems.

name: Propose and justify alternatives with trade‑off analysis
definition: Comments present feasible alternatives and explain their reasonableness (e.g., statutory fit), analyzing expected benefits, costs, and other impacts or trade‑offs.

name: Provide concrete, decision‑relevant data and examples
definition: Supply on‑the‑ground data, concrete examples, and operational evidence tied to claims, with enough fields to enable agency analysis.

name: Provide quantitative impact and compliance‑cost estimates
definition: Provide quantified impact and cost estimates with transparent, verifiable assumptions and underlying calculations.

name: Public alerting systems: reliability, resilience, and user controls
definition: Design alerting architectures for resilience/redundancy and reliability; balance guaranteed vs. best‑effort delivery; and provide appropriate user customizations consistent with alerting goals.

name: Reasoned, record‑supported justification
definition: Decisions provide a reasoned explanation grounded in the rulemaking record and credible evidence, including why alternatives were rejected.

name: Regulatory coordination and consistency
definition: Coordinate and harmonize across agencies and jurisdictions (including internationally) to reduce duplication and burdens while preserving flexibility and coherence.

name: Responsible AI principles: safety, fairness, accountability, and transparency
definition: Adopt operational standards for AI that ensure safety/effectiveness, prevent discrimination, and require transparency/explainability, accountability, and appropriate protections (especially in sensitive domains).

name: Section‑specific engagement and preservation for review
definition: Cite exact sections/pages, state requested changes with reasons and evidence, and frame issues precisely to preserve them for agency consideration and potential judicial review.

name: Sourcing, citations, and evidentiary reliability
definition: Provide complete, verifiable citations; corroborate important or doubtful points; ensure underlying data and sources are reliable and personally reviewed where appropriate.

name: Submission accuracy and evidence‑based claims
definition: Keep submissions on‑point and jurisdictionally appropriate; verify facts; rebut inaccurate claims; and prioritize evidence‑based assertions (including for AI‑assisted drafting).

name: Substantive, non‑duplicative comments (not vote‑counting)
definition: Avoid form letters and bare support/opposition; provide self‑contained, substantive input responsive to the proposal.

name: Tailor and mitigate burdens for small entities
definition: Assess and reduce disproportionate burdens on SMEs and small jurisdictions by scaling or tailoring requirements.

name: Term length and rotation for accountability
definition: Use short terms, frequent elections, or rotation to maintain officials’ dependence on and responsiveness to the people.

name: Transparency and disclosure of regulatory actions and performance
definition: Adopt high standards for timely, accurate, and substantive public disclosures (e.g., plans, fees, supervisory processes, periodic/material reports, incident transparency, and voting behavior).

name: Transparency and public information for participation and oversight
definition: Provide timely, affordable, and accessible information and public justifications (including appropriate meeting/interaction disclosures) so the public can participate effectively and exercise oversight.

name: Tribal sovereignty and meaningful consultation
definition: Honor the government‑to‑government relationship and trust responsibility through respectful, high‑quality consultation when tribal rights or interests are implicated.

name: Use specific personal or community impact stories
definition: Include first‑hand, practitioner, or community narratives with concrete, verifiable details (e.g., dates, places, examples) to document human impacts.

name: User fees: transparency, reasonableness, and non‑discrimination
definition: Disclose and justify fees; design cost allocations that are reasonable and equitable among beneficiaries/users; ensure any differentials are reasonable and not unfairly discriminatory.

name: Workforce transition, reskilling, and quality jobs
definition: Mitigate displacement from technological/green transitions, promote creation of quality jobs, support reskilling, and ensure equitable participation and labor protections.
